title: The present tense
description: Make the present of any verb, use the everyday irregulars, and use one form for now, habits and plans.

guide.summary: The Swedish present is the easiest tense you will meet: one form for every person, ending in -r. This page shows the three ways that -r is added, the few irregular verbs you use all the time, when a verb stays in the infinitive, and the jobs the present does: now, habits and plans.

sections.title: One form for everyone
sections.text: Swedish verbs do not change with the person. Jag, du, han, hon, vi, ni and de all take the same present form, and it almost always ends in -r.
steps: Find the verb and its infinitive.
Make the present form once; the subject does not matter.
Check it ends in -r.

examples.sv: Jag talar svenska och de talar engelska.
examples.en: I speak Swedish and they speak English.

watch: No -s for he or she, and no special plural form: de bor, like jag bor.
The infinitive, without -r, is not a present form.

sections.title: The -ar group: keep the -a, add -r
sections.text: Most Swedish verbs, and nearly every new one, keep the whole infinitive and add -r.
steps: Check the dictionary: the present form is listed first.
If it ends in -ar, keep the infinitive and add -r.

examples.en: I am waiting for the bus.

watch: You cannot see the group from the infinitive alone: tala and köpa both end in -a. Learn the present with the verb.

sections.title: The -er group: drop the -a, add -er
sections.text: A large group drops the final -a and adds -er. If the stem already ends in r, nothing more is added.
steps: Remove the -a to find the stem.
Add -er.
If the stem ends in r, as kör- does, add nothing.
watch: Köpar, läsar and drickar do not exist.
Kör, not körer: two r sounds are not written.

sections.title: Short verbs ending in a vowel: add -r
sections.text: Short verbs whose infinitive ends in a vowel other than -a just add -r.
steps: See that the infinitive ends in a vowel like o or å.
Add -r and nothing else.
watch: No -ar and no -er: boar and troer are wrong.

sections.title: Everyday verbs to know by heart
sections.text: A handful of very common verbs are worth learning as words of their own. Vara, göra and veta are irregular; ha, säga and gå follow the patterns above but are so common that you should know them at once. All have one form for every person.
steps: Recognise one of the six verbs.
Use its form from the table, whoever the subject is.
watch: Säger keeps its g in writing, even though you hear sejer.
Varar, görer and veter do not exist.

sections.title: When the verb stays in the infinitive
sections.text: Only one verb per clause carries the present. A verb after att, or after kan, vill, måste or ska, stays in the infinitive. Those four take no att.
steps: Find the verb that carries the present ending.
Put any verb after kan, vill, måste or ska in the infinitive, without att.
Put any verb after att in the infinitive.
watch: English want to becomes vill with no att.
Never two -r forms side by side: kan simmar is wrong.

sections.title: What the present is used for
sections.text: One form covers English I speak, I am speaking and often I am going to speak. Swedish has no -ing tense, so never put är in front of another verb.
steps: Use the plain present for now and for habits.
For a plan, the present plus a time word like imorgon is enough.
Never add är before the verb.

examples.sv: Just nu tittar jag på en film.
examples.en: Right now I am watching a film.

examples.sv: Vi åker till Göteborg på fredag.
examples.en: We are going to Gothenburg on Friday.

watch: Jag är dricker is a direct copy of English I am drinking and is wrong.
Imorgon is also written i morgon.

steps: Find the verb.
Make its present form; it is the same for every subject.
Check it ends in -r and is not the infinitive.
Check the verb belongs to the -ar group.
Keep the infinitive and add -r.
Check the verb belongs to the -er group.
Drop the -a and add -er.
If the stem ends in r, add nothing.
See that the infinitive ends in a vowel other than -a.
Add only -r.
Recognise vara, ha, göra, veta, säga or gå.
Use the form from the table for every person.
Find the verb that carries the present.
Put a verb after att, kan, vill, måste or ska in the infinitive.
Leave out att after kan, vill, måste and ska.
Decide whether it is now, a habit or a plan.
Use the plain present in all three.
Do not put är before the verb.

exercises.hint: Swedish has one present form for every person. What is it for prata?
exercises.feedback: The present ends in -r whoever the subject is.
exercises.explanation: Vi pratar: the same form as jag pratar, du pratar and de pratar.

mistakes.why: That is the infinitive, the dictionary form. With a subject in front, the verb needs its present ending -r.
An -s ending is not a plural marker on Swedish verbs; it makes a different, passive form. We takes the same form as I.
That is the past tense, for something that already happened.

exercises.hint: Plural subjects get no special ending in Swedish.
exercises.feedback: De takes exactly the form jag would take.
exercises.explanation: De bor i en lägenhet: bo + -r, the same form for every person.

mistakes.why: Bo is the infinitive. A verb after a subject like de needs the present ending.
Bo already ends in a vowel, so it takes only -r; -ar belongs to verbs whose infinitive ends in -a.
There is no plural form of the verb in Swedish: they lives and I live use the same word.

exercises.hint: One present form serves every subject, plural ones too.
exercises.feedback: The present of tala is the same for vi as for jag.
exercises.explanation: Vi talar svenska hemma: tala + -r.

mistakes.why: Tala is the infinitive. A subject like vi needs the present form ending in -r.
The -s form is passive, roughly is spoken. It is not a plural ending.
Talade is the past tense. Hemma here describes how things are now, so the present is needed.

exercises.instruction: Change jag to de. Keep the verb right.
exercises.hint: Does the verb change when the subject changes in Swedish?
exercises.feedback: Only the subject changes; the verb stays exactly as it is.
exercises.explanation: De dricker kaffe på morgonen: dricker is the form for every person.

mistakes.why: Dricka belongs to the -er group, and changing the subject never moves a verb into another group.
Dricka is the infinitive. Plural subjects still take the present form with -r.
The subject has not been changed yet: the sentence should start with they.

exercises.hint: We is vi. The verb is bo, and its present form is the same as for I.
exercises.feedback: Use the present of bo, which ends in -r.
exercises.explanation: Vi bor i Stockholm: one present form for all persons.

mistakes.why: Bo is the infinitive. In the present the verb takes -r, even after vi.
Towns take i, not på: you live in a city.

exercises.hint: They is de. Choose the verb tile with the present ending.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the bare infinitive.
exercises.explanation: De jobbar hemma: jobba + -r, the same form as jag jobbar.

mistakes.why: Jobba is the infinitive. A plural subject does not drop the ending; every person takes the -r form.

exercises.hint: Tala ends in -a. Keep the whole infinitive and add one letter.
exercises.feedback: Verbs of the -ar group add -r to the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Jag talar: tala + -r.

mistakes.why: Tala keeps its -a in the present; -er belongs to verbs like köpa and läsa, which drop the -a.
That is the infinitive. In the present the verb needs -r.
Only one r is added: the -a of the infinitive is already there.

exercises.hint: Spela is an -ar verb: keep the -a.
exercises.feedback: Add -r to the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Han spelar fotboll varje vecka: spela + -r.

mistakes.why: Spela belongs to the -ar group and keeps its -a. The -er ending is for another group.
That is the infinitive. After a subject like han the verb needs -r.
The -s form is passive. Han is doing the playing himself.

exercises.hint: Lyssna ends in -a and belongs to the biggest group.
exercises.feedback: The -ar group keeps the whole infinitive and adds -r.
exercises.explanation: Jag lyssnar på musik: lyssna + -r. Lyssna takes på before what you listen to.

mistakes.why: Lyssna keeps its -a in the present. Dropping it is what -er verbs do.
Lyssna is the infinitive, used after att or a verb like kan. A subject needs the present.
The -s form is passive, roughly is listened to. Here the speaker is the one listening.

exercises.hint: Laga ends in -a and keeps it in the present.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile has the -er ending of another group.
exercises.explanation: Hon lagar middag: laga + -r.

mistakes.why: Laga belongs to the -ar group, so the -a stays. Lager is not a form of this verb.

exercises.hint: Look at the verb. Which group does städa belong to?
exercises.feedback: Städa is an -ar verb: keep the -a and add -r.
exercises.explanation: Vi städar huset idag: städa + -r.

mistakes.why: The verb is unchanged. Städa keeps its -a in the present.
Städa is the infinitive; with vi in front the present form needs -r.

exercises.source: I am waiting for the bus.
exercises.hint: Swedish has no am waiting: one present form covers it. For is på after vänta.
exercises.feedback: Use the present of vänta, an -ar verb.
exercises.explanation: Jag väntar på bussen: vänta + -r, and vänta takes på.

mistakes.why: Swedish builds no tense with är and a verb. The present form alone means am waiting.
Vänta keeps its -a in the present; it belongs to the -ar group.
Vänta takes på, not för, before what you wait for.

exercises.hint: Köpa is an -er verb: drop the -a, then add -er.
exercises.feedback: Remove the final -a and add -er.
exercises.explanation: Du köper: köp- + -er.

mistakes.why: Köpa is not an -ar verb. Its -a falls away and -er comes in its place.
That is the infinitive. A subject needs the present form.
Only verbs ending in a vowel sound like bo add a bare -r. Köp- ends in a consonant and needs -er.

exercises.hint: Läsa drops its -a and adds -er, for every person.
exercises.feedback: The -er group: stem läs- + -er.
exercises.explanation: De läser: läs- + -er, the same form as jag läser.

mistakes.why: Läsa belongs to the -er group, so its -a does not stay.
That is the infinitive. A plural subject still takes the present form.
Swedish verbs have no plural ending: they read and I read are the same word.

exercises.hint: Skriva works like läsa.
exercises.feedback: Drop the -a and add -er.
exercises.explanation: Hon skriver ett brev: skriv- + -er.

mistakes.why: Skriva is an -er verb, so its -a is dropped rather than kept.
That is the infinitive. After hon the verb takes its present ending.
A bare -r follows a vowel. Skriv- ends in a consonant, so the ending is -er.

exercises.hint: Dricka is an -er verb. The subject is plural, but that changes nothing.
exercises.feedback: Drop the -a of dricka and add -er.
exercises.explanation: Barnen dricker mjölk till frukost: drick- + -er.

mistakes.why: Dricka belongs to the -er group. Keeping the -a and adding -r is the pattern of verbs like tala.
Dricka is the infinitive. Barnen is the subject, so the verb takes its present form.

exercises.hint: Köra has a stem that already ends in -r.
exercises.feedback: When the stem ends in -r, the -er ending adds nothing you can hear or write.
exercises.explanation: Pappa kör bil till jobbet: kör- already ends in r, so nothing is added.

mistakes.why: The stem kör- already ends in r, so the -er ending merges into it and is not written twice.
Köra is an -er verb, not an -ar verb, and its stem already ends in r.

exercises.instruction: Remove vill and put the verb in the present.
exercises.hint: Without vill, köpa needs its own present ending.
exercises.feedback: Köpa drops its -a and adds -er.
exercises.explanation: Jag köper bröd: köp- + -er.

mistakes.why: Without vill the verb is no longer an infinitive; it needs the present ending.
Köpa belongs to the -er group, so its -a is dropped.
Vill is still there. The sentence should say what I buy, not what I want to buy.

exercises.hint: Which group does läsa belong to?
exercises.feedback: Läsa drops its -a and adds -er.
exercises.explanation: Han läser tidningen varje morgon: läs- + -er.

mistakes.why: The verb has not been fixed. Läsa does not keep its -a in the present.
Läsa is the infinitive. After han the present form is needed.

exercises.hint: Bo ends in a vowel that is not -a. Add one letter.
exercises.feedback: Short verbs ending in a vowel add just -r.
exercises.explanation: Jag bor: bo + -r.

mistakes.why: Bo has no -a to keep: the -ar ending belongs to verbs like tala.
-er comes after a consonant. Bo ends in a vowel, so the ending is only -r.
That is the infinitive. The present needs -r.

exercises.hint: Förstå ends in the vowel å.
exercises.feedback: Add -r straight to the vowel.
exercises.explanation: Jag förstår inte svenska: förstå + -r.

mistakes.why: Förstå ends in a vowel, so it takes only -r, not -er.
That is the infinitive; after jag the verb needs -r.
There is no -a to keep: förstå ends in å, and only -r is added.

exercises.hint: Bo ends in a vowel: add the shortest ending.
exercises.feedback: Short vowel verbs add only -r.
exercises.explanation: Var bor du?: bo + -r. The verb comes before du in a question.

mistakes.why: Bo does not end in -a, so it cannot take the -ar ending.
-er is for stems ending in a consonant. Bo ends in a vowel.
Bo is the infinitive. A question with du still needs the present form.

exercises.hint: Tro ends in a vowel. Pick the tile with just -r added.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile adds -ar to a verb that has no -a.
exercises.explanation: Jag tror det: tro + -r. Swedish says I believe it where English says I think so.

mistakes.why: Tro ends in o, not -a, so the -ar ending does not belong to it.

exercises.hint: Look at the verb. What does bo add in the present?
exercises.feedback: Bo adds only -r.
exercises.explanation: Min mamma bor i Göteborg: bo + -r.

mistakes.why: The verb is unchanged. Bo has no -a, so -ar is wrong.
-er follows consonant stems; bo ends in a vowel.

exercises.hint: Vara is the most irregular verb. Its present looks nothing like the infinitive.
exercises.feedback: The present of vara is a short word of its own.
exercises.explanation: Jag är: vara is irregular, and the same form serves every person.

mistakes.why: Vara does not follow the -ar group. Its present has to be learnt as a separate word.
That is the infinitive, used after att or a verb like kan.
Var is the past tense, I was.

exercises.hint: Göra loses its last letter in the present.
exercises.feedback: The present of göra is one syllable.
exercises.explanation: De gör: göra drops the -a, and since gör- ends in r nothing is added.

mistakes.why: The stem gör- already ends in r, so the -er ending is not written.
Göra is not an -ar verb; its present is short.
That is the infinitive. A subject needs the present.

exercises.hint: Säga behaves like an -er verb in the present. Its g is silent in speech, but it is written.
exercises.feedback: Drop the -a and add -er.
exercises.explanation: Han säger: säg- + -er. It sounds like sejer but keeps its g in writing.

mistakes.why: Säga is not an -ar verb. Its -a falls away in the present.
That is the infinitive. After han the verb needs its present form.
That spells the spoken sound. The written form keeps the ä and the g of säga.

exercises.hint: Ha is short and ends in a vowel: it just adds -r.
exercises.feedback: Ha adds -r like bo does.
exercises.explanation: Vi har en hund: ha + -r.

mistakes.why: Ha is the infinitive. With vi in front, the present form is needed.
Haver is an old form you may see in songs or older texts. Today only the short form is used.
Only one -r is added to ha; the a is not doubled.

exercises.hint: Göra has a short, one-syllable present.
exercises.feedback: The present of göra drops the -a and adds nothing.
exercises.explanation: Vad gör du idag?: the verb comes before du in a question.

mistakes.why: Göra does not take the -ar ending. Its present is shorter than the infinitive.
Göra is the infinitive; a question with du needs the present.
The stem gör- already ends in r, so -er is not added.

exercises.hint: Tired describes her. Which verb means is?
exercises.feedback: Describing someone needs the present of vara.
exercises.explanation: Hon är trött idag: vara is irregular, and its present is a short word of its own.

mistakes.why: Vara is the infinitive, the dictionary form. A subject needs the present.
Vara does not follow the -ar pattern. Its present must be learnt by heart.
Har means has. Swedish says she is tired, as English does.

exercises.hint: Going on foot is gå. Towards home is hem, not hemma.
exercises.feedback: Use the present of gå: no am or are in front.
exercises.explanation: Vi går hem nu: gå + -r. Nu går vi hem is also right, with the verb kept second.

mistakes.why: Gå is the infinitive. The present takes -r.
Hemma means at home. Movement towards home uses hem.
Swedish has no tense built with är and a verb. The present alone means are going.

exercises.instruction: Change jag to hon. Keep the verb right.
exercises.hint: Changing the subject never changes a Swedish verb.
exercises.feedback: Only the pronoun changes.
exercises.explanation: Hon vet inte: vet is the present of veta for every person.

mistakes.why: Veta is irregular: its present is short and takes no -er.
Veta is the infinitive. After hon the present is needed.
The subject has not been changed to she yet.

exercises.hint: Swedish drops en before a job after is.
exercises.feedback: One tile is the infinitive of the verb.
exercises.explanation: Han är läkare: the present of vara, and no article before a job.

mistakes.why: Vara is the infinitive. After han the verb needs its present form, which is irregular.

exercises.hint: Only one verb in the sentence carries the present ending.
exercises.feedback: After kan, the next verb stays in the infinitive, with no att.
exercises.explanation: Jag kan tala svenska: kan is already in the present, so the second verb is the bare infinitive.

mistakes.why: Kan already carries the present. The verb after it stays in the dictionary form.
Kan, vill, måste and ska are followed directly by the infinitive, never by att.

exercises.instruction: Write the right form of åka.
exercises.hint: Vill is the verb with the ending. What comes after it?
exercises.feedback: After vill, use the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Vi vill åka till Stockholm: vill + infinitive.

mistakes.why: Vill already carries the present. A second verb after it does not take -er.
Vill is followed directly by the infinitive, without att.

exercises.hint: Two verbs stand side by side. Which one keeps its ending?
exercises.feedback: Only måste carries the tense; jobba goes back to the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Hon måste jobba idag: måste + infinitive.

mistakes.why: The sentence is unchanged. After måste the second verb has no present ending.
Måste is followed directly by the infinitive, with no att in between.

exercises.hint: Kan takes the present ending. What happens to simmar?
exercises.feedback: After kan, the verb goes back to the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Han kan simma bra: kan + infinitive.

mistakes.why: Only one verb carries the present ending. After kan, simma loses its -r.
Kan is followed directly by the infinitive, without att.

exercises.hint: Want is vill. English to disappears after it.
exercises.feedback: Vill + infinitive, with no att.
exercises.explanation: Jag vill dricka vatten: vill carries the present, dricka stays in the infinitive.

mistakes.why: English says want to, but Swedish vill takes the infinitive directly. Att is left out.
After vill the second verb stays in the infinitive.

exercises.hint: Tycker om is followed by att and then the infinitive.
exercises.feedback: After att, choose the dictionary form.
exercises.explanation: Hon tycker om att läsa: att + infinitive, like English to read.

mistakes.why: After att the verb stays in the infinitive, ending in -a.

exercises.source: Just nu ____ jag på en film.
exercises.hint: Swedish has no separate am doing form.
exercises.feedback: The plain present describes what is happening right now.
exercises.explanation: Just nu tittar jag på en film: the present alone means I am watching.

mistakes.why: Swedish never puts är before another verb to make a tense. The present alone covers am watching.
Titta is the infinitive. The sentence needs the present form.

alternatives.message: Correct: ska also gives the future. This exercise practises the plain present.

exercises.hint: A plan for tomorrow can use the plain present, with a time word.
exercises.feedback: The present plus imorgon is enough for the near future.
exercises.explanation: Jag åker imorgon: the present with a time word describes a planned future. Imorgon is also written i morgon.

mistakes.why: Swedish builds no tense with är and a verb. The present alone means am leaving.
Åka is the infinitive. The sentence needs the present form.

exercises.hint: There is no is reading in Swedish: one form covers it.
exercises.feedback: Use the plain present of läsa.
exercises.explanation: Hon läser en bok: the present for something happening right now.

mistakes.why: Är cannot stand in front of another verb to make an -ing tense. Leave it out.
English is reading has no copy in Swedish. Use one verb in the present.

exercises.hint: One word is copied from English am drinking.
exercises.feedback: Remove är: the present alone means am drinking.
exercises.explanation: Jag dricker kaffe nu: one present form for now.

mistakes.why: The sentence is unchanged. Swedish has no tense made of är and a verb.
Är should go, not the ending of the verb.

alternatives.message: Ska åka is correct Swedish for a plan, but here write the plain present of åka.

exercises.hint: På fredag points to a plan. Swedish often uses the plain present for it.
exercises.feedback: The present with a time word gives the near future.
exercises.explanation: Vi åker till Göteborg på fredag: åk- + -er, a planned trip.

mistakes.why: Åka is the infinitive. Without ska or a similar verb, the present form is needed.
Åka belongs to the -er group, so its -a is dropped.

exercises.hint: Habits use the plain present. Leave out the tile that means are.
exercises.feedback: One tile is a form of vara, which is not needed.
exercises.explanation: Vi äter frukost varje dag: the present for a habit.

answers: Vi är äter frukost varje dag.
mistakes.why: Är cannot be added in front of another verb. The present alone describes a habit.
